title: Route the PIN active digit and the restore-wizard letter row through the constant-time secret glyph path on a forced frame, and pin it with a regression test
threat: EM/power probe on the NV3007 SPI stream or on the MCU during PIN entry / seed restore. Each PIN commit screen paints exactly one secret digit at a known cell through the address-keyed public font (legacy) or the non-forced Item::Text run (px, strip-digest skip + 64-bit digest of secret pixels left in `static mut SHOWN`); eight screens = the PIN. The restore wizard letter row leaks every typed seed letter the same way (#784). This is the same channel F-24/F-27 closed for the word pages — TVLA on the legacy scan measured 650.90 leaky vs 0.00 CT.
proposal: (1) Legacy: in `pin_entry::render_pin_screen` and `seed_wizard::render_letter_screen` build the secret row via `secret_text::secret_glyph_cols` and emit it with `flush_with_secret_rows` instead of `draw_line`+`flush`. (2) px: make `status_map::pin_row` / `letter_row` emit the active digit / typed letters as `Item::Secret` cells (placeholders in the record, bytes passed as `secret`) and call `screens::show_with(&row, &secret)` so `play_screen` sets `force = true` (present_frame_ex streams every strip, records no digest, invalidates SHOWN). Extend `Font::blit_secret_run`'s candidate range from a-z to a-z + 0-9 (or a second numeric run) for the digit. (3) Add the host test #784 recommends: every Screen produced by pin_row/letter_row/seed_page/candidate_list that carries a secret is presented with a non-empty `secret` (force=true) and never through `show()`. (4) Also re-randomise the start digit of the NEXT position after each accepted digit (Trezor caesar `set_page_counter(get_random_digit_position())`), not once per session.
rationale: Cheapest, highest-certainty fix on the surface: the CT primitives, the forced-frame discipline and the host-test scaffolding already exist; only two call sites and one builder still bypass them. The PIN is the key to the device and the restore letters are the seed itself — both are strictly more valuable than the word pages that are already protected.
repo_evidence: secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:177-210 (render_pin_screen: px `show(&row)` at 182-186; legacy `row1[col] = b'0' + d` at 200-201 then `d.draw_line(1, ...)` → public_glyph_cols)
secure/src/ui/px/status_map.rs:276-293 (pin_row: `glyphs[i] = b'0' + pin[i] % 10` into an Entry record, Item::Text)
secure/src/ui/px/status_map.rs:296-317 (letter_row: `glyphs[i] = buf[i]` for committed and active letters)
secure/src/ui/seed_wizard.rs:911-916 (render_letter_screen px branch calls `screens::show`, not `show_with`) and :918-935 (legacy branch draws letters via draw_line)
secure/src/ui/px/lcd.rs:663 (`let force = !secret.is_empty()`) and :304-322 (present_frame_ex: digest skip unless forced)
secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:55-60 (F-20 start digits drawn once at session start, never re-randomised per digit)
gh #784 OPEN priority:medium (letter row); PIN active digit is NOT tracked by any issue
vendor_precedent: Trezor core caesar PIN: fresh random digit position after every accepted digit (core/embed/rust/src/ui/layout_caesar/component/input_methods/pin.rs:320-328). Trezor crypto/bip39.c constant-time word lookup (commit 9b1c06205c). Ledger 1.6/2023 inverted-digit PIN UI (LSB-006, new-pin-screen).
risks: blit_secret_run currently scans 26 lowercase glyphs; adding digits widens the scan (~36 candidates per pixel) and the cost per forced PIN frame rises; must keep black_box barriers (secret_text.rs:44-50 documents the LLVM-fold regression). Per-digit re-randomisation changes the F-20 UX slightly (user re-dials from a new start each position) — already the case per position, so minimal. Must also verify with `make e2e-px` so the change is compiled IN (ui-px path), not only the legacy path.
